Question Choices: Select. When solving a system of two linear equations in two variables, valid elimination removes one variable and leaves only the identity $3=3$. The original equations each describe a line. Does the system have infinitely many solutions? ~~True | False~~
Hints: Use equivalent line equations: identical lines, distinct parallel lines, or one intersection.
Solution: A reversible elimination step leaves an identity, so one line equation is redundant. Every point on the remaining line solves both equations; there are infinitely many ordered-pair solutions. Requested answer: True.
